[CHANGELOG.md: v1.4.0 (2026-09-15)]
- Add daily click counts per link, kept for 400 days.
- Add the trusted_proxies setting, so the real client address is used
  behind a reverse proxy.
- Add a read-only admin page at /admin, off by default.

[CHANGELOG.md: v1.3.0 (2026-08-02)]
- Add per-client rate limiting.
- Add webhooks for link.created, link.deleted, and link.expired.
- Run database migrations automatically at startup.
- Fix a redirect loop when a short link points to itself.

[CHANGELOG.md: v1.2.0 (2026-05-14)]
- Add link expiry: a link can be created with an expires_at time.
- Add custom short codes, given in the slug field.
- Add `shortlink links import` and `shortlink links export` for CSV.

[CHANGELOG.md: v1.1.0 (2026-03-03)]
- Add the JSON API for creating links.
- Add API keys with read, write, and admin scopes.
- Serve a health check at /healthz.
- Write logs as JSON by default; set log_format to text for the old
  format.

[CHANGELOG.md: v1.0.0 (2026-01-12)]
- First release: redirects, the `shortlink links` commands, SQLite
  storage, Prometheus metrics on metrics_addr, and an in-memory link
  cache.

[CONTRIBUTING.md: Building]
shortlink is a single Go package tree. The main package is in `cmd/shortlink`; the rest of the code is under `internal/`: `internal/store` (SQLite), `internal/redirect`, `internal/api`, `internal/limit` (rate limiting), `internal/clicks`, `internal/hooks` (webhooks), and `internal/admin`.

Building needs Go 1.26 or later. To install the latest code:

```sh
go install example.com/shortlink/cmd/shortlink@latest
```

Release binaries exist for linux/amd64, linux/arm64, and darwin/arm64, so you only need to build from source when you are changing it.

[CONTRIBUTING.md: Building]
To run what you built, use the settings in `config/defaults.yaml`. Any setting can be overridden by an environment variable of the same name in capitals, with dots turned into underscores: `rate_limit.burst` becomes `RATE_LIMIT_BURST`. Check the configuration before starting:

```sh
shortlink check-config
shortlink serve
```

The server stores links in one SQLite file, `shortlink.db` by default. Run one process per database file; two processes on one file fail with "database is locked".

[CONTRIBUTING.md: Tests and linting]
Both must pass before a change is merged:

```sh
go test ./...
golangci-lint run
```

[CONTRIBUTING.md: Pull requests]
- Every pull request that changes behavior adds a `CHANGELOG` entry under "Unreleased".
- Every bug fix comes with a test.
- Commits are signed off:

```sh
git commit -s
```

[CONTRIBUTING.md: Reporting security problems]
Report vulnerabilities to security@shortlink.example. Do not open a public issue. Expect a reply within 3 working days.

[CONTRIBUTING.md: Documentation]
User-facing behavior is described in the files under `docs/`: `docs/api.md`, `docs/deploy.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`, and `docs/rate-limits.md`. If your change alters what an operator or developer does with shortlink, update the matching file in the same pull request.

[README.md: shortlink]
shortlink is a small URL shortener written in Go. It stores links in
SQLite, in a single file named shortlink.db by default, and serves
redirects and a JSON API from one binary.

Start it with `go run ./cmd/shortlink`. Settings come from
config/defaults.yaml; see docs/configuration.md for every setting and
how to override it.

- docs/short-codes.md: generated and custom codes, and what a target may be
- docs/redirects.md: how short URLs redirect

[docs/admin.md: The admin page]
The admin page is a read-only view of the links in the database. It is
off by default and lives at /admin on `listen_addr` (`:8080` by
default). It arrived in v1.4.0.

[docs/admin.md: Turning it on]
Set `admin.enabled` in config/defaults.yaml, or override it with an
environment variable of the same name in capitals:

```yaml
admin:
  enabled: true
```

```sh
ADMIN_ENABLED=true shortlink serve
```

Run `shortlink check-config` to confirm the configuration loads.

[docs/admin.md: Setting the password]
`admin.password_hash` is not written by hand. Run this on the server
and enter the password at the prompt:

```sh
shortlink admin set-password
```

The command stores the hash in `admin.password_hash`. shortlink keeps
only the hash, so the password cannot be recovered from the
configuration. Run the command again to change the password.

[docs/admin.md: What it shows]
Everything on the page is read-only. You can:

- Search links.
- See each link's daily click counts.

You cannot create, edit, or delete links there. To change links, use
the JSON API or the `shortlink links` commands; see api.md. Daily click
counts are kept for `clicks.retention_days` (400 by default), so the
page does not show counts older than that.

[docs/admin.md: Logging in]
Sign in with the password set by `shortlink admin set-password`. A login
lasts 12 hours, after which you sign in again.

[docs/admin.md: Protecting /admin]
The page is served on `listen_addr` under /admin, the same port as
redirects and the API, so it is reachable wherever that port is
reachable. Put it behind the access controls of your reverse proxy as
well, for example HTTP basic auth or an IP allowlist in nginx or Caddy.
See deploy.md for the proxy setup.

If you also run shortlink behind a proxy that sets X-Forwarded-For,
list the proxy in `trusted_proxies` so rate limiting sees the real
client address.

[docs/admin.md: Example]
```yaml
listen_addr: :8080
database: shortlink.db
admin:
  enabled: true
  password_hash: "$2a$10$..."   # set by `shortlink admin set-password`
```

Then start the server and open http://localhost:8080/admin.

[docs/analytics.md: Analytics]
Since v1.4.0, shortlink counts clicks per link per day. Daily counts are
kept for clicks.retention_days days, 400 by default, and then deleted.
The total click count for a link is kept for as long as the link exists.

GET /api/links/{code}/clicks returns the daily counts that are still
kept, oldest first.

[docs/api-keys.md: API keys]
API keys are the only credentials the JSON API accepts. They are made and managed with the `shortlink keys` commands on the server; there is no API endpoint for creating them.

[docs/api-keys.md: Creating a key]
```sh
shortlink keys create --name ci-bot --scope write
```

The name is yours to choose and is only for recognising the key later in `shortlink keys list`. The scope is one of `read`, `write`, or `admin`.

The command prints the key once, at creation. Copy it then; the server never shows it again.

[docs/api-keys.md: What a key looks like]
A key starts with `sl_` and continues with its random characters. Send it in the Authorization header as a bearer token:

```text
Authorization: Bearer sl_...
```

The server stores only the SHA-256 hash of the key. If you lose a key, create a new one and revoke the old one.

[docs/api-keys.md: Scopes]
| Scope | Allows |
| --- | --- |
| read | GET requests |
| write | GET requests, plus creating and deleting links |
| admin | Everything write allows, plus reading every link's clicks across the server |

Pick the narrowest scope that fits. A key used from CI that only creates links does not need `admin`.

[docs/api-keys.md: Listing keys]
```sh
shortlink keys list
```

This shows each key's id, name, and scope, not the key itself.

[docs/api-keys.md: Revoking a key]
```sh
shortlink keys revoke 3
```

The argument is the key's id, as printed by `shortlink keys list`. A revoked key is rejected with 401 from the next request on. Revoke a key as soon as it is no longer needed, and immediately if you think it has been copied.

[docs/api-keys.md: When a request is rejected]
A request with a missing, wrong, or revoked key gets `401 Unauthorized`. A valid key whose scope doesn't allow the request gets `403 Forbidden`: a key with `read` scope gets 403 on a request to create or delete a link, and a key with `write` scope gets 403 on a request for every link's clicks. Either way the JSON body has an `error` field, as described in docs/api.md.

A `429` is not a key problem; it means the client is over its rate limit. See rate-limits.md.

[docs/api.md: The JSON API]
Every request needs an API key in the Authorization header:
`Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys are created with
`shortlink keys create` on the server; a read key can only make GET
requests (see docs/api-keys.md).

[docs/api.md: Read and delete a link]
GET /api/links/{code} returns the link and its total clicks.
DELETE /api/links/{code} removes it; its short URL then returns 404.

[docs/api.md: Errors]
Errors come back as JSON with an error field:

- 400: the body was not valid, or the target was refused.
- 401: the API key was missing, wrong, or revoked.
- 403: the key's scope doesn't allow the request.
- 409: the slug is already in use.
- 429: the client is over its rate limit (see rate-limits.md).

[docs/architecture.md: Code layout]
shortlink is one binary. Each part of it lives in its own package under `internal/`, except for the entry point:

[docs/architecture.md: Code layout]
| Package | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `cmd/shortlink` | Entry point. Parses the command line, loads configuration, opens the database, applies migrations, and starts the server. `shortlink` with no command runs `shortlink serve`. |
| `internal/store` | SQLite storage. Owns the `links`, `clicks_daily`, `api_keys`, and `schema_version` tables and the database file (`shortlink.db` by default) in WAL mode. |
| `internal/redirect` | Resolves short codes and answers redirects with `redirect_status`, applying `append_query` to the target. |
| `internal/api` | The JSON API under `/api`, and the request checks that go with it: URL length, `blocked_domains`, slug rules. |
| `internal/limit` | Per-client rate limiting: `rate_limit.requests_per_minute` with `rate_limit.burst` on top. |
| `internal/clicks` | Click counting. Holds counts in memory and writes them to `clicks_daily`. |
| `internal/hooks` | Webhooks: signing, delivery, and retries. |
| `internal/admin` | The read-only admin page served at `/admin`. |

[docs/architecture.md: Code layout]
The same process also answers `/healthz` and, on `metrics_addr`, `/metrics`. Migrations run automatically when the server starts; `shortlink migrate` applies them by hand.

[docs/architecture.md: A redirect request]
1. `internal/limit` rates the client. The client address comes from the connection, or from the `X-Forwarded-For` header when the peer is listed in `trusted_proxies` (see docs/deploy.md). Over the limit returns 429 and increments `shortlink_rate_limited_total`.
2. `internal/redirect` looks the code up in the in-memory cache, if `cache_size` is not 0. A hit adds to `shortlink_cache_hits_total`, a miss to `shortlink_cache_misses_total`, and the miss falls through to the database.
3. `internal/store` returns the link. A missing code, a reserved code (`api`, `admin`, `healthz`, `metrics`), or a link past its `expires_at` returns 404.
4. `internal/redirect` answers with `redirect_status` (302 by default) and, with `append_query` true, copies the short URL's query string onto the target. A `HEAD` request gets the same answer as `GET` but goes no further: no click is counted.
5. `internal/clicks` adds one click to its in-memory counts, bots included. Counts are written to `clicks_daily` every `clicks.flush_interval` (5 seconds), so a new click appears in the API within about 5 seconds and a crash can lose up to 5 seconds of counts. A normal shutdown flushes first.

[docs/architecture.md: An API request]
1. `internal/limit` rates the client as for a redirect.
2. `internal/api` reads the `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header and asks `internal/store` to match it against the `api_keys` table. The store compares the SHA-256 hash of the presented key. A missing, wrong, or revoked key is 401; a valid key whose scope doesn't allow the request is 403.
3. The key's scope decides what is allowed: `read` for GET, `write` for creating and deleting links, `admin` for reading every link's clicks across the server.
4. The handler validates the body in `internal/api`: targets must be `http` or `https` and no longer than `max_url_length` (2048 bytes), a domain in `blocked_domains` is refused with 400 and the error "domain blocked", a `slug` is 3 to 32 characters of letters, digits, and hyphens, and a slug already in use is 409 Conflict. Codes are generated by the store at `code_length` from letters and digits, minus `0`, `O`, `1`, `l`, and `I`.
5. `internal/store` writes or reads the link. A link's target cannot be changed: delete it and create it again with the same slug.
6. For `link.created` and `link.deleted`, `internal/hooks` POSTs a JSON body to `webhooks.url` when that setting is set. Each request carries `X-Shortlink-Signature: sha256=<hex>`, an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body keyed with `webhooks.secret`. Delivery failures are retried up to 5 attempts in all, waiting 1s, 2s, 4s, and 8s between them; after the last failure the event is logged and dropped, and `shortlink_webhook_failures_total` goes up. `link.expired` is sent the same way. See docs/webhooks.md.
7. `internal/api` answers with JSON. Errors carry an `error` field: 400 for an invalid body, 401 for a missing, wrong, or revoked key, 403 for a scope that doesn't allow the request, 409 for a slug in use, 429 for the rate limit.

[docs/architecture.md: Logging]
Every request, redirect or API, produces one line with `log_format` (JSON by default): `method`, `path`, `status`, `duration_ms`, `client_ip`, `request_id`. An incoming `X-Request-ID` header is used as the `request_id`; otherwise shortlink makes one and returns it in the same header.

[docs/cli.md: Command line reference]
Every command reads config/defaults.yaml. Any setting can be overridden by an
environment variable of the same name in capitals, with dots replaced by
underscores: `rate_limit.burst` becomes `RATE_LIMIT_BURST`.

[docs/cli.md: shortlink serve]
Run the server. `shortlink` with no command does the same thing. It serves
redirects, the JSON API (see api.md), and, when `admin.enabled` is true, the
admin page at /admin. Metrics are served on metrics_addr, separate from
listen_addr.

```sh
shortlink serve
```

[docs/cli.md: shortlink check-config]
Load the configuration, report errors, and exit. Use it after changing
config/defaults.yaml or setting environment variables.

```sh
shortlink check-config
```

[docs/cli.md: shortlink migrate]
Apply database migrations to the file given by `database` and exit. Since
v1.3.0 migrations also run automatically when the server starts, so you only
need this when upgrading from v1.2.0 or earlier:

```sh
shortlink migrate
```

Back up the database first; see deploy.md.

[docs/cli.md: shortlink version]
Print the version of the binary.

```sh
shortlink version
```

[docs/cli.md: shortlink links add `<url>`]
Create a link and print its short URL. `--slug name` sets a custom short code
(3 to 32 characters, letters, digits, and hyphens); a slug already in use is
refused with 409 Conflict. `--expires 2027-01-01T00:00:00Z` sets the expiry
time. The target must be an http or https URL no longer than
`max_url_length`, and its domain must not be in `blocked_domains`.

```sh
shortlink links add https://example.com/a/long/path --slug launch --expires 2027-01-01T00:00:00Z
```

[docs/cli.md: shortlink links list]
List every link.

```sh
shortlink links list
```

[docs/cli.md: shortlink links delete `<code>`]
Remove one link. Its short URL then returns 404.

```sh
shortlink links delete x7Kp2
```

[docs/cli.md: shortlink links import `<file.csv>`]
Read a CSV file with a header row and the columns url, slug, expires_at; slug
and expires_at may be empty. Rows are checked like API requests. A bad row is
reported with its line number and skipped, and the rest are imported.

```sh
shortlink links import links.csv
```

[docs/cli.md: shortlink links export]
Write CSV to standard output: a header row, then code, url, expires_at,
created_at, total_clicks for every link.

```sh
shortlink links export > links.csv
```

[docs/cli.md: shortlink keys create `--name <name> --scope read|write|admin`]
Create an API key. The key starts with `sl_` and is shown once, at creation;
the server stores only its SHA-256 hash. Scopes are cumulative: `read` allows
GET requests, `write` also creates and deletes links, `admin` also reads every
link's clicks across the server.

```sh
shortlink keys create --name ci --scope write
```

[docs/cli.md: shortlink keys list]
List keys with their names, ids, and scopes.

```sh
shortlink keys list
```

[docs/cli.md: shortlink keys revoke `<id>`]
Revoke a key. It is rejected with 401 from the next request on.

```sh
shortlink keys revoke 3
```

[docs/cli.md: shortlink admin set-password]
Prompt for the admin password and store its hash in `admin.password_hash`.
Set `admin.enabled` true to serve the page at /admin on listen_addr, and put
it behind the proxy's access controls as well (see deploy.md). A login lasts
12 hours. The page is read-only: search links and view each link's daily
clicks.

```sh
shortlink admin set-password
```

For webhooks, rate limiting, and click counting, see docs/webhooks.md,
docs/rate-limits.md, and docs/analytics.md.

[docs/configuration.md: Configuration]
shortlink reads config/defaults.yaml at startup. Any setting can be
overridden with an environment variable of the same name in capitals:
listen_addr becomes LISTEN_ADDR, and dots become underscores, so
rate_limit.burst becomes RATE_LIMIT_BURST.
Run `shortlink check-config` to load the configuration and report any
errors without starting the server.

[docs/configuration.md: Configuration]
| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| listen_addr | :8080 | Address for redirects, the API, and /admin |
| metrics_addr | :9090 | Address for /metrics; empty turns metrics off |
| database | shortlink.db | The SQLite file |
| base_url | http://localhost:8080 | The start of every short URL |
| code_length | 5 | Length of generated short codes |
| redirect_status | 302 | 302 (temporary) or 301 (permanent) |
| append_query | true | Append the short URL's query string to the target |
| max_url_length | 2048 | Longest target URL accepted, in bytes |
| blocked_domains | (none) | Target domains refused when a link is created |
| cache_size | 10000 | Links kept in the in-memory cache; 0 turns it off |
| rate_limit.requests_per_minute | 120 | Requests allowed per client per minute |
| rate_limit.burst | 20 | Extra requests allowed in a short burst |
| trusted_proxies | (none) | Proxy addresses whose X-Forwarded-For header is believed |
| clicks.retention_days | 400 | How long daily click counts are kept |
| clicks.flush_interval | 5s | How often counted clicks are written to the database |
| webhooks.url | (none) | Where webhook events are sent; empty turns them off |
| webhooks.secret | (none) | Key for signing webhook bodies |
| admin.enabled | false | Serve the admin page at /admin |
| admin.password_hash | (none) | Set by `shortlink admin set-password` |
| log_format | json | json or text |
| log_level | info | debug, info, warn, or error |
| read_timeout | 5s | Longest time to read a request |
| write_timeout | 10s | Longest time to write a response |
| shutdown_timeout | 15s | Time allowed for requests in flight when stopping |

[docs/database.md: The database]
shortlink keeps everything in one SQLite file. The `database` setting
names it (`shortlink.db` by default) and can be overridden with the
`DATABASE` environment variable. The container image keeps its database
in the /data volume, so set `DATABASE=/data/shortlink.db` there. SQLite
runs in WAL mode. All storage goes through `internal/store`.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| database | shortlink.db | The SQLite file |
| clicks.retention_days | 400 | How long daily click counts are kept |

[docs/database.md: Tables]
| Table | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| links | Every link: its short code, target URL, creation time, and expiry time |
| clicks_daily | Daily click counts per link, kept for clicks.retention_days (400 days by default) |
| api_keys | API keys by name and scope, plus revocation state and each key's SHA-256 hash |
| schema_version | Which migrations have been applied to this file |

Only the hash of an API key is stored, never the key itself. A link's
target cannot be changed after the link is created; delete the link and
create it again with the same slug.

[docs/database.md: Migrations]
Since v1.3.0 migrations run automatically when the server starts. The
`shortlink migrate` command applies them by hand and exits:

```sh
shortlink migrate
```

Use it to migrate without starting the server, and when upgrading from
v1.2.0 or earlier: those databases predate automatic migrations, so run
`shortlink migrate` with the new binary before starting it.

Migrations only go forward. Downgrading after a migration is not
supported; restore a backup instead. Back up before every upgrade.

[docs/database.md: One process per database file]
Run one shortlink process per database file. A second process pointed at
the same file fails with "database is locked". If you need more than one
instance, give each its own `database` file.

[docs/database.md: Supported databases]
SQLite is the only supported database. The file named by `database` is
the whole datastore.

[docs/database.md: Backups]
The database is a single SQLite file, but copying it directly can catch
it partway through a write. Back it up with the SQLite backup command
while the server runs:

```sh
sqlite3 shortlink.db ".backup backup.db"
```

Back up the database before every upgrade, and before running
`shortlink migrate` by hand. If an upgrade or a migration has to be
undone, stop the server and put the backup back in place as the database
file; run one process per database file as usual.

[docs/deploy.md: Deploying shortlink]
shortlink is one static binary. Copy it to the server with
config/defaults.yaml and run it under a process supervisor such as
systemd.

[docs/deploy.md: Behind a reverse proxy]
When shortlink runs behind a reverse proxy such as nginx, every request
appears to come from the proxy's address, so every user shares one rate
limit. List the proxy's address in trusted_proxies; shortlink then takes
the client's address from the X-Forwarded-For header that the proxy
adds.

[docs/deploy.md: Backups]
The database is a single SQLite file. Back it up with
`sqlite3 shortlink.db ".backup backup.db"` while the server runs;
copying the file directly can catch it partway through a write.

[docs/faq.md: Why does shortlink use SQLite?]
All links live in one SQLite file, shortlink.db by default, in WAL mode. There is no separate database server to install or keep in step with shortlink, and a backup is one command while the server runs:

```sh
sqlite3 shortlink.db ".backup backup.db"
```

See deploy.md for backup notes.

[docs/faq.md: Can shortlink use Postgres?]
No. Storage is SQLite only, in a single file set by the database setting. Other databases are not supported. Run one process per database file.

[docs/faq.md: Can I change where a link points?]
No. A link's target is fixed when the link is created. To repoint a short code, delete the link and create it again with the same slug:

```sh
shortlink links delete x7Kp2
shortlink links add https://example.com/new/path --slug x7Kp2
```

Deleting first matters: a slug already in use gets 409 Conflict. The codes api, admin, healthz, and metrics are reserved. Note that after a redirect_status of 301, browsers that already visited the link may keep going to the old target (see below).

[docs/faq.md: Are clicks unique visitors?]
No. Each redirect counts one click, bots included. The counts tell you how often a short URL was followed, not how many different people followed it. Daily counts per link are kept for clicks.retention_days (400 days). HEAD requests are answered like GET but do not count a click.

[docs/faq.md: Why does a link still redirect after I deleted it?]
If redirect_status is 301, browsers cache the redirect and keep going to the old target even after the link is deleted or expires. 302 (the default) is not cached that way. Use 301 only for links that never change.

[docs/faq.md: How soon do clicks show up?]
Within about 5 seconds. Clicks are held in memory and written to the database every clicks.flush_interval (5s by default), so a new click appears in the API after roughly that long. A crash can lose up to 5 seconds of counts; a normal shutdown writes them first. GET /api/links/{code} in api.md returns a link's total clicks.

[docs/faq.md: How do I run more than one server process?]
Run one process per database file. Two shortlink processes sharing one SQLite file fail with "database is locked". Give each process its own database setting and its own file. If you are running shortlink behind a reverse proxy, see deploy.md for trusted_proxies, and see troubleshooting.md for the locked-database error.

[docs/faq.md: Where do I report a security problem?]
Report vulnerabilities to security@shortlink.example, not in public issues. Expect a reply within 3 working days.

[docs/import-export.md: CSV import and export]
shortlink reads and writes links as CSV, since v1.2.0. Both commands use the configured database (the `database` setting) and run on the server.

[docs/import-export.md: Importing links]
```sh
shortlink links import links.csv
```

The file needs a header row with the columns `url`, `slug`, `expires_at`. `slug` and `expires_at` may be empty, in which case a short code is generated and the link never expires. `expires_at` takes a time such as `2027-01-01T00:00:00Z`.

```csv
url,slug,expires_at
https://example.com/a/long/path,,
https://example.com/summer-sale,summer,2027-01-01T00:00:00Z
```

A slug is 3 to 32 characters of letters, digits, and hyphens. The codes `api`, `admin`, `healthz`, and `metrics` are reserved.

[docs/import-export.md: Importing links]
Rows are checked like API requests: targets must be `http` or `https` URLs no longer than `max_url_length` (2048 bytes), and a target on a domain listed in `blocked_domains` is refused. A bad row is reported with its line number and skipped; the rest of the file is imported.

If you see "database is locked", another process is using the same file. Run one process per database file (see troubleshooting.md).

[docs/import-export.md: Exporting links]
```sh
shortlink links export > links.csv
```

`shortlink links export` writes CSV to standard output, with a header row and the columns `code`, `url`, `expires_at`, `created_at`, `total_clicks` for every link:

```csv
code,url,expires_at,created_at,total_clicks
x7Kp2,https://example.com/a/long/path,,2026-05-14T10:02:00Z,1841
aB3-kL,https://example.com/summer-sale,2027-01-01T00:00:00Z,2026-05-20T09:15:00Z,42
```

`total_clicks` comes from the database, so a click counted in the last `clicks.flush_interval` (5 seconds) may not be in the output yet.

[docs/import-export.md: Moving links between servers]
Export on the old server and import on the new one:

```sh

[docs/import-export.md: old server]
shortlink links export > links.csv

[docs/import-export.md: new server]
shortlink links import links.csv
```

The export and import columns are not the same. Import takes `url`, `slug`, `expires_at`, while export writes `code`, `url`, `expires_at`, `created_at`, `total_clicks`. To move links as they are, rename `code` to `slug` and drop `created_at` and `total_clicks`:

```csv
url,slug,expires_at
https://example.com/a/long/path,x7Kp2,
https://example.com/summer-sale,aB3-kL,2027-01-01T00:00:00Z
```

Keeping the same slug keeps the same short code on the new server. Check these before importing:

[docs/import-export.md: new server]
- `base_url` on the new server sets the start of every short URL. If it differs from the old server, the links keep their codes but the host changes.
- A code already in use on the new server is a bad row: it is reported with its line number and skipped. Delete the existing link first if you want the imported one (see docs/api.md and the `shortlink links` commands).
- Click counts are not carried over. `total_clicks` starts over on the new server, and the export file has no daily counts to import.

Back up the database on both servers before and after a move; see deploy.md.

[docs/install.md: Installing shortlink]
shortlink is one static binary. It needs a SQLite file for its database and serves plain HTTP; TLS is terminated at a reverse proxy such as nginx or Caddy (see deploy.md).

[docs/install.md: Release binaries]
Download the archive for your platform from the releases page. Binaries are published for linux/amd64, linux/arm64, and darwin/arm64. Unpack it somewhere on the server and run the binary directly or under a process supervisor such as systemd.

[docs/install.md: go install]
With Go 1.26 or later installed:

```sh
go install example.com/shortlink/cmd/shortlink@latest
```

This puts `shortlink` in your Go binary directory.

[docs/install.md: Container image]
The image is `shortlink/shortlink`. It keeps its database in the `/data` volume, so set `DATABASE=/data/shortlink.db` and mount the volume, or the database disappears with the container:

```sh
docker run --name shortlink -p 8080:8080 \
  -v shortlink-data:/data \
  -e DATABASE=/data/shortlink.db \
  shortlink/shortlink
```

Any setting can be given as an environment variable of the same name in capitals, with dots turned into underscores. `rate_limit.burst` becomes `RATE_LIMIT_BURST`; `database` becomes `DATABASE`, as above.

[docs/install.md: First run]
Copy `config/defaults.yaml` next to the binary and check the configuration before starting anything:

```sh
shortlink check-config
```

It loads the configuration, reports errors, and exits. Fix anything it points out, then start the server:

```sh
shortlink serve
```

`shortlink` with no command does the same thing as `shortlink serve`.

The settings you are most likely to change on a first run:

| Setting | Default | Change it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| listen_addr | :8080 | the port is taken |
| base_url | http://localhost:8080 | the server is reachable under a public address |
| database | shortlink.db | the SQLite file belongs somewhere else |

[docs/install.md: First run]
`base_url` is the start of every short URL shortlink hands out, so set it to the address people will actually use. The database is one SQLite file; run one process per database file.

[docs/install.md: Checking it works]
The health check is at /healthz. Ask for it on the listen port:

```sh
curl -i http://localhost:8080/healthz
```

If the server answers, it is up and taking requests. Your first short URL is `base_url` plus the short code; with the defaults, a link with the code `x7Kp2` is `http://localhost:8080/x7Kp2`.

Metrics are served separately on `metrics_addr` (`:9090` by default), which keeps `/metrics` off the public port.

Create your first link with the CLI or the JSON API (see docs/api.md):

```sh
shortlink links add https://example.com/a/long/path
```

If something does not behave as expected, see docs/troubleshooting.md. For backups and reverse proxy setup, see docs/deploy.md.

[docs/logging.md: Logging]
shortlink writes one log line per request. Since v1.1.0 the default is
JSON (`log_format` json); earlier logs were text. Both formats carry
the same fields.

[docs/logging.md: Settings]
| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| log_format | json | `json` or `text` |
| log_level | info | `debug`, `info`, `warn`, or `error` |

Set them in config/defaults.yaml or override with environment
variables: `LOG_FORMAT=text`, `LOG_LEVEL=debug`.

[docs/logging.md: Request log fields]
Each request line has these fields:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| method | HTTP method of the request |
| path | Request path |
| status | Response status code |
| duration_ms | Time taken to answer, in milliseconds |
| client_ip | Client address, from X-Forwarded-For when the request comes from a trusted proxy (see deploy.md) |
| request_id | ID of the request, see below |

A JSON line looks like this:

```json
{"method":"GET","path":"/x7Kp2","status":302,"duration_ms":2,"client_ip":"203.0.113.9","request_id":"a1b2c3d4"}
```

The text format prints the same fields on one line, for reading in a
terminal when you set `LOG_FORMAT=text`.

[docs/logging.md: Request IDs]
Every request has a request ID. If the client sends an X-Request-ID
header, shortlink uses its value as the request_id in the log line. If
there is no such header, shortlink makes one and returns it in the
X-Request-ID response header, so the value is in the log either way.

Pass an ID you generate yourself when you want to follow one request
through a proxy, shortlink, and anything else that logs it. The same
ID appears in shortlink's log line and in the header you sent or
received.

[docs/logging.md: Levels]
`log_level` sets the lowest level logged: `debug`, `info`, `warn`, or
`error`. Request lines are logged at `info`, so with the default
`log_level` info every request is logged. Set `LOG_LEVEL=warn` to log
warnings and errors only.

[docs/logging.md: Related]
- Metrics live on a separate port, metrics_addr (`:9090` by default);
  see docs/metrics.md.
- Webhook delivery failures are logged and counted in
  `shortlink_webhook_failures_total` (see webhooks.md).
- Shutdown behavior is covered in docs/performance.md: a normal stop
  writes pending click counts before the process exits.

[docs/metrics.md: Metrics]
shortlink serves Prometheus metrics on a separate port. Set that port with
metrics_addr (:9090 by default):

```yaml
metrics_addr: ":9090"
```

The endpoint is /metrics on metrics_addr. It is on its own port so that
metrics stay off the public port where redirects, the API, and /admin are
served. Point Prometheus at the metrics port only; do not expose it through
the reverse proxy that fronts the public port. Set metrics_addr to an empty
value to turn metrics off.

Override the port with an environment variable if needed:

```sh
METRICS_ADDR=":9191" shortlink serve
```

[docs/metrics.md: Metric names]
| Metric | Type | What it counts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| shortlink_redirects_total{status} | counter | Redirects served, by response status |
| shortlink_api_requests_total{method,code} | counter | API requests, by HTTP method and response code |
| shortlink_rate_limited_total | counter | Requests rejected because the client was over its rate limit |
| shortlink_cache_hits_total | counter | Link lookups answered from the in-memory cache |
| shortlink_cache_misses_total | counter | Link lookups that reached the database |
| shortlink_links | gauge | Links currently stored |
| shortlink_webhook_failures_total | counter | Webhook events dropped after their last retry failed |

[docs/metrics.md: Metric names]
Cache metrics only move when the cache is on (cache_size above 0). With the
cache off, lookups always go to the database and these counters stay flat.
shortlink_webhook_failures_total goes up once per event that has used all 5
delivery attempts (see docs/webhooks.md).

[docs/metrics.md: Example queries]
Rate of rate-limited requests over the last 5 minutes:

```promql
rate(shortlink_rate_limited_total[5m])
```

Cache hit ratio over the last 5 minutes. It is 1 when every lookup is served
from the cache:

```promql
rate(shortlink_cache_hits_total[5m])
  /
(rate(shortlink_cache_hits_total[5m]) + rate(shortlink_cache_misses_total[5m]))
```

Redirects per second, by status:

```promql
sum by (status) (rate(shortlink_redirects_total[5m]))
```

API errors (non-2xx responses) per second:

```promql
sum(rate(shortlink_api_requests_total{code!~"2.."}[5m]))
```

[docs/metrics.md: Notes]
shortlink_links is a gauge, not a counter: it rises and falls as links are
created, deleted, or expired, so use `shortlink_links` directly rather than
`rate()`.

For the request logs behind these numbers, see docs/logging.md; each request line carries method, path, status, and duration_ms. For
deployment details such as reverse proxies and backups, see docs/deploy.md.

[docs/performance.md: Measured redirect rates]
On a 2-vCPU virtual machine, shortlink serves about 9,000 redirects a second with the cache on and about 2,500 with it off. The numbers are a single-instance measurement on SQLite, not a benchmark of your hardware.

[docs/performance.md: The link cache]
shortlink keeps recently used links in memory so a redirect does not need a database read. The cache holds `cache_size` links (10,000 by default) and drops the least recently used entry when it is full. Set `cache_size` to 0 to turn the cache off.

```yaml
cache_size: 10000
```

Or with an environment variable:

```sh
CACHE_SIZE=0 shortlink serve
```

Watch how the cache behaves with `shortlink_cache_hits_total` and `shortlink_cache_misses_total` on `metrics_addr` (see metrics.md).

[docs/performance.md: Database size]
SQLite has been tested to 10 million links. Use the settings in config/defaults.yaml as a starting point and measure on your own hardware before relying on any rate here.

[docs/performance.md: Click counting]
Each redirect counts one click. Counts are held in memory and written to the database every `clicks.flush_interval` (5 seconds by default):

```yaml
clicks:
  flush_interval: 5s
  retention_days: 400
```

This batching has two consequences:

- **Freshness**: a new click shows up in the API within about 5 seconds of the redirect. Raise or lower `clicks.flush_interval` to trade write frequency against how stale the counts look.
- **Crashes**: a crash can lose up to one flush interval of counts. A normal shutdown writes them first, so stopping the server with SIGTERM keeps every count it has taken.

Daily click counts are kept for `clicks.retention_days` (400 by default).

[docs/performance.md: Timeouts]
Three timeouts bound how long requests can take. Tune them in config/defaults.yaml or by environment variable:

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| read_timeout | 5s | Longest time to read a request |
| write_timeout | 10s | Longest time to write a response |
| shutdown_timeout | 15s | Time allowed for requests in flight when stopping |

```yaml
read_timeout: 5s
write_timeout: 10s
shutdown_timeout: 15s
```

```sh
SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT=30s shortlink serve
```

`shutdown_timeout` applies when the server stops. shortlink waits up to this long for in-flight requests to finish and writes out counted clicks before exiting. Give it longer than the slowest response you expect to serve.

[docs/performance.md: Where to look next]
- rate-limits.md covers per-client request limits.
- metrics.md lists the Prometheus metrics available on `metrics_addr`.
- troubleshooting.md covers rate limits that hit everyone at once and the "database is locked" error.

[docs/rate-limits.md: Rate limits]
Each client, identified by its IP address, may make
rate_limit.requests_per_minute requests a minute (120 by default), plus
a short burst of rate_limit.burst more (20 by default).

A client over its limit gets 429 Too Many Requests, with a Retry-After
header giving the number of seconds to wait. Redirects count against
the limit too, so a link shared widely from one office network can
exhaust that network's limit.

[docs/redirects.md: Redirects]
A short URL answers with a redirect to its target. The status code and the
final target URL are controlled by two settings in config/defaults.yaml,
overridable by environment variables of the same name in capitals
(REDIRECT_STATUS, APPEND_QUERY).

[docs/redirects.md: Status codes]
| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| redirect_status | 302 | 302 (temporary) or 301 (permanent) |

302 is the safe choice and the default. Browsers follow it every time and
re-ask shortlink where the link goes.

301 is cached by browsers. After a 301, a browser that has visited the link
keeps going to the old target even after the link is deleted or expires, and
even after you change redirect_status back. Use 301 only for links that never
change, since a shortened link cannot have its target edited later
(see api.md).

[docs/redirects.md: Query strings]
With append_query true (the default), the query string of the short URL is
added to the target's own query string. Given the target
`https://example.com/a/long/path`:

```text
GET /x7Kp2?ref=mail
Location: https://example.com/a/long/path?ref=mail
```

Set append_query false to drop the short URL's query string and redirect to
the target exactly as it was stored. The setting is global, not per link.

[docs/redirects.md: HEAD requests]
A HEAD request is answered like a GET: the same status code and Location
header. It does not count a click. Use HEAD when a client only wants to know
where a short URL points.

[docs/redirects.md: Deleted and expired links]
A short URL whose link has been deleted or whose expires_at time has passed
returns 404. Expiry is checked on each request, so a link stops redirecting at
its expires_at time; a link created with an expires_at already in the past is
expired immediately (see troubleshooting.md).

Remember the 301 warning above: a browser that cached a permanent redirect may
keep going to the old target even after the link returns 404.

[docs/redirects.md: Click counting]
Every redirect counts one click, including requests from bots. Counts are not
unique visitors; the same client following a link twice counts twice. A HEAD
request does not count.

Counts are held in memory and written to the database every
clicks.flush_interval (5s by default):

- A new click shows up in the API within about 5 seconds.
- A crash can lose up to 5 seconds of counts. A shutdown that finishes
  normally writes the pending counts first.

[docs/redirects.md: Click counting]
Daily counts per link are kept for clicks.retention_days (400 by default).
Read them with GET /api/links/{code}/clicks (see docs/analytics.md) or on the
admin page (see docs/admin.md). The
shortlink_redirects_total{status} metric on metrics_addr counts redirects by
status code.

[docs/security.md: TLS at the proxy]
shortlink serves plain HTTP. Terminate TLS at a reverse proxy such as nginx or Caddy and point clients at the proxy. See deploy.md for the proxy setup.

When shortlink runs behind a proxy, every request appears to come from the proxy's address unless you tell it otherwise. List the proxy's address in trusted_proxies; shortlink then takes the client's address from the X-Forwarded-For header the proxy adds. That address is what rate limiting and request logs use, so only trust proxies you control.

[docs/security.md: API keys]
Create keys only on the server, with the narrowest scope that works:

```sh
shortlink keys create --name ci --scope write
```

A key starts with `sl_` and is shown once, at creation. The server stores only its SHA-256 hash, so a lost key cannot be recovered; create a new one and revoke the old one with `shortlink keys revoke <id>`. Treat keys like passwords: pass them in the Authorization header and keep them out of source control and shell history.

Scopes are read (GET requests), write (also create and delete links), and admin (also read every link's clicks across the server). A revoked key is rejected with 401 from the next request on.

[docs/security.md: API keys]
The admin password is separate from API keys. Set it with `shortlink admin set-password`, which stores its hash; a login lasts 12 hours.

[docs/security.md: Target URLs]
Targets must be http or https URLs no longer than max_url_length (2048 bytes). Refuse whole domains when you create links by listing them in blocked_domains; a link to one of those domains is refused with 400 and the error "domain blocked". The check runs when a link is created, so review blocked_domains before importing links in bulk with `shortlink links import`.

The codes api, admin, healthz, and metrics are reserved and can't be used as slugs. A slug already in use gets 409 Conflict.

[docs/security.md: Target URLs]
With redirect_status 302 (the default), deleting a link or letting it expire stops the redirect at once. With 301, browsers cache the target and keep going there even after the link is deleted or expires. Use 301 only for links that never change.

[docs/security.md: Metrics and the admin page]
Prometheus metrics are served on metrics_addr (`:9090` by default), on a separate port from listen_addr. Keep that port off the public internet: bind it to a private interface or block it at the firewall. Set metrics_addr to an empty value to turn metrics off.

The admin page is off by default (admin.enabled false). It is read-only, but it shows links and their daily clicks, so put it behind the proxy's access controls as well as its own password. It is served on listen_addr under /admin.

[docs/security.md: Webhook signing]
If you use webhooks, set webhooks.secret and verify each delivery at the receiver. Every request carries `X-Shortlink-Signature: sha256=<hex>`, an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body keyed with webhooks.secret. Compute the same HMAC over the body you received and compare it to the header. See docs/webhooks.md for the event payloads.

[docs/security.md: Reporting vulnerabilities]
Report vulnerabilities to security@shortlink.example, not in public issues. Expect a reply within 3 working days.

[docs/short-codes.md: Short codes]
Every link has a short code. The code is either generated for you or given
by you as `slug` when the link is created. It is the last part of the short
URL, built from base_url: `https://sl.example/x7Kp2` has the code `x7Kp2`.

[docs/short-codes.md: Generated codes]
By default a code is code_length characters long, 5, drawn from letters and
digits. The look-alike characters `0`, `O`, `1`, `l`, and `I` are left out,
so a code typed from a screenshot or read aloud is less likely to be
mistaken for another one. Change code_length in config/defaults.yaml if 5
is too short or too long; shorter codes run out sooner as links pile up.

To create a link from the command line:

```sh
shortlink links add https://example.com/a/long/path
```

[docs/short-codes.md: Custom codes]
Give a code with the `--slug` flag:

```sh
shortlink links add https://example.com/a/long/path --slug launch
```

or with the `slug` field when creating a link through the API (see
docs/api.md). A slug must be 3 to 32 characters and may contain letters,
digits, and hyphens.

If the slug is already in use, the request fails with 409 Conflict. Pick
another slug, or delete the existing link first:

```sh
shortlink links delete launch
```

The codes `api`, `admin`, `healthz`, and `metrics` are reserved and cannot
be used as slugs.

[docs/short-codes.md: Target rules]
The target of a link is a URL, with these rules:

- It must use the http or https scheme.
- It must be no longer than max_url_length, 2048 bytes by default.
- Its domain must not be listed in blocked_domains.

A target that breaks a rule is refused when the link is created. A blocked
domain gets 400 with the error `domain blocked`. Set blocked_domains in
config/defaults.yaml to refuse whole domains you never want shortened.

[docs/short-codes.md: Why a target cannot be changed]
A link's target is fixed at creation. There is no update operation, so a
short code that has been printed, mailed, or posted always points where it
pointed when it was made. That keeps a shared short URL stable: nobody can
retarget it later and send existing readers somewhere else.

To point a code somewhere new, delete the link and create it again with the
same slug:

```sh
shortlink links delete launch
shortlink links add https://example.com/new/path --slug launch
```

[docs/short-codes.md: Why a target cannot be changed]
This only works while the code is free, so do the two steps close together.
Before deleting, check redirect_status in config/defaults.yaml. With 301
the old target may be cached by browsers that have already visited the
link, and those browsers keep going there even after the link is deleted or
recreated; see docs/redirects.md. With the default 302, browsers pick up
the new target on their next visit.

[docs/troubleshooting.md: A new link returns 404]
If the link was created with an expires_at time that has already
passed, it is expired from the moment it is created, and its short URL
returns 404. Check the expires_at value, including its time zone.

[docs/troubleshooting.md: Every user hits the rate limit at once]
shortlink is probably behind a proxy and sees every request as coming
from the proxy's address. Set trusted_proxies; see deploy.md.

[docs/troubleshooting.md: "database is locked"]
Two shortlink processes are using the same SQLite file. Run one process
per database file.

[docs/upgrading.md: Upgrading shortlink]
Back up the database before you upgrade. Migrations run automatically when the server starts, and a migration can change the database in ways you cannot undo; the backup is what you go back to.

[docs/upgrading.md: Before you start]
Don't copy the SQLite file directly. Back it up with the SQLite backup command while the server runs (see deploy.md):

```sh
sqlite3 shortlink.db ".backup backup.db"
```

Copying the file with `cp` can catch it partway through a write. If shortlink runs in the container image shortlink/shortlink, run the backup inside the container against the database in the /data volume.

[docs/upgrading.md: Step by step]
1. Back up the database:

```sh
   sqlite3 shortlink.db ".backup backup.db"
   ```

2. If you are upgrading from v1.2.0 or earlier, run the new binary's migrate command first (see below).

3. Replace the binary with the new one, or pull the new container image.

4. Restart the server with `shortlink serve`.

5. Migrations run at startup. Confirm the new version with `shortlink version`.

[docs/upgrading.md: Upgrading from v1.2.0 or earlier]
Automatic migrations arrived in v1.3.0. A database written by v1.2.0 or earlier predates them, so run the migrate command with the new binary before you start the server:

```sh
shortlink migrate
```

Then start the server as usual. `shortlink migrate` applies the migrations and exits; it is safe to run on any version, since a database that is already current has nothing left to apply.

[docs/upgrading.md: After the upgrade]
Run `shortlink check-config` with the new binary to confirm the configuration still loads. New releases may add settings with defaults (see config/defaults.yaml), so a configuration file from an older version keeps working without edits.

[docs/upgrading.md: Downgrading]
Downgrading after a migration is not supported. Older binaries do not know about tables or columns added by newer migrations, and there is no command that removes them. To go back to an older version, stop the server and restore the backup you took before upgrading:

```sh
sqlite3 shortlink.db ".restore backup.db"
```

Then run the older binary against the restored file. Keep the backup until you are sure the new version is working.

[docs/webhooks.md: Webhooks]
Since v1.3.0, shortlink can notify an HTTP endpoint when a link changes.

[docs/webhooks.md: Turning webhooks on]
Set `webhooks.url` and `webhooks.secret` in config/defaults.yaml, or the
environment variables of the same name in capitals:

```yaml
webhooks:
  url: https://ops.example/hooks/shortlink
  secret: 6f1c2f4d0a8b4e1c9f0a3b7c5d2e8f11
```

```sh
WEBHOOKS_URL=https://ops.example/hooks/shortlink
WEBHOOKS_SECRET=6f1c2f4d0a8b4e1c9f0a3b7c5d2e8f11
```

An empty `webhooks.url` turns webhooks off. The same secret is used to
sign every delivery, so keep it in sync with your receiver.

[docs/webhooks.md: Events]
shortlink POSTs a JSON body for three events:

| Event | Sent when |
| --- | --- |
| `link.created` | A link is created |
| `link.deleted` | A link is deleted |
| `link.expired` | A link passes its `expires_at` time |

A delivery for `link.expired` looks like this:

```json
{
  "event": "link.expired",
  "code": "x7Kp2",
  "url": "https://example.com/a/long/path",
  "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

Treat any 2xx response as accepted. A delivery that does not get a 2xx
within 10 seconds is treated as failed.

[docs/webhooks.md: Verifying a signature]
Each request carries the header `X-Shortlink-Signature: sha256=<hex>`,
an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body keyed with `webhooks.secret`. To
verify it:

1. Read the raw body bytes first, before parsing them as JSON.
2. Compute HMAC-SHA256 over those bytes with `webhooks.secret`.
3. Compare the hex digest with the part of the header after `sha256=`,
   using a constant-time comparison. Reject the request if they differ.

[docs/webhooks.md: Retries]
A failed delivery is retried, up to 5 attempts in all. The waits
between attempts are 1s, 2s, 4s, and 8s.

After the last failure shortlink logs the event and drops it. It is not
kept for later delivery. Each dropped event increments the counter
`shortlink_webhook_failures_total` on the metrics port
(metrics_addr, `:9090` by default); see metrics.md for the full list.

input: What does a 429 response mean, and which header says when to retry?

Passages:

[docs/rate-limits.md: Rate limits]
Each client, identified by its IP address, may make
rate_limit.requests_per_minute requests a minute (120 by default), plus
a short burst of rate_limit.burst more (20 by default).

A client over its limit gets 429 Too Many Requests, with a Retry-After
header giving the number of seconds to wait. Redirects count against
the limit too, so a link shared widely from one office network can
exhaust that network's limit.

[docs/api.md: Errors]
Errors come back as JSON with an error field:

- 400: the body was not valid, or the target was refused.
- 401: the API key was missing, wrong, or revoked.
- 403: the key's scope doesn't allow the request.
- 409: the slug is already in use.
- 429: the client is over its rate limit (see rate-limits.md).

[docs/api-keys.md: When a request is rejected]
A request with a missing, wrong, or revoked key gets `401 Unauthorized`. A valid key whose scope doesn't allow the request gets `403 Forbidden`: a key with `read` scope gets 403 on a request to create or delete a link, and a key with `write` scope gets 403 on a request for every link's clicks. Either way the JSON body has an `error` field, as described in docs/api.md.

A `429` is not a key problem; it means the client is over its rate limit. See rate-limits.md.

[docs/webhooks.md: Retries]
A failed delivery is retried, up to 5 attempts in all. The waits
between attempts are 1s, 2s, 4s, and 8s.

After the last failure shortlink logs the event and drops it. It is not
kept for later delivery. Each dropped event increments the counter
`shortlink_webhook_failures_total` on the metrics port
(metrics_addr, `:9090` by default); see metrics.md for the full list.

Each redirect counts one click. Counts are held in memory and written to the database every `clicks.flush_interval` (5 seconds by default):

```yaml
clicks:
```

- It must be no longer than max_url_length, 2048 bytes by default.

[docs/redirects.md: Status codes]
| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| redirect_status | 302 | 302 (temporary) or 301 (permanent) |

302 is the safe choice and the default. Browsers follow it every time and
re-ask shortlink where the link goes.

301 is cached by browsers. After a 301, a browser that has visited the link
keeps going to the old target even after the link is deleted or expires, and
even after you change redirect_status back. Use 301 only for links that never
change, since a shortened link cannot have its target edited later
(see api.md).

[docs/faq.md: Can I change where a link points?]
No. A link's target is fixed when the link is created. To repoint a short code, delete the link and create it again with the same slug:

```sh
shortlink links delete x7Kp2
shortlink links add https://example.com/new/path --slug x7Kp2
```

Deleting first matters: a slug already in use gets 409 Conflict. The codes api, admin, healthz, and metrics are reserved. Note that after a redirect_status of 301, browsers that already visited the link may keep going to the old target (see below).

[docs/short-codes.md: Why a target cannot be changed]
A link's target is fixed at creation. There is no update operation, so a
short code that has been printed, mailed, or posted always points where it
pointed when it was made. That keeps a shared short URL stable: nobody can
retarget it later and send existing readers somewhere else.

To point a code somewhere new, delete the link and create it again with the
same slug:

```sh
shortlink links delete launch
shortlink links add https://example.com/new/path --slug launch
```

[docs/short-codes.md: Why a target cannot be changed]
This only works while the code is free, so do the two steps close together.
Before deleting, check redirect_status in config/defaults.yaml. With 301
the old target may be cached by browsers that have already visited the
link, and those browsers keep going there even after the link is deleted or
recreated; see docs/redirects.md. With the default 302, browsers pick up
the new target on their next visit.

However, [docs/redirects.md: Status codes] warns that `301` responses are cached by browsers: after visiting a 301 link, a browser keeps going to the old target even after the link is deleted or expires, and even if you change `redirect_status` back. It recommends 301 only for links that never change, since a link's target cannot be edited after creation (see [docs/faq.md: Can I change where a link points?]).

If you do need to repoint a link, [docs/short-codes.md: Why a target cannot be changed] says to delete the link and recreate it with the same slug, but notes that with a cached 301, browsers that already visited the link may keep going to the old target. With the default 302, browsers pick up the new target on their next visit.

If redirect_status is 301, browsers cache the redirect and keep going to the old target even after the link is deleted or expires. 302 (the default) is not cached that way. Use 301 only for links that never change.

## Answer

The most likely cause is a **cached permanent redirect**. If `redirect_status` is set to **301**, browsers cache the redirect and continue going to the old target even after the link has been deleted or expired.

So the short link isn't actually still redirecting on the server — it returns 404 (per docs/redirects.md) — but browsers that cached a 301 keep resolving to the old target. The documented fix is to use 302 (the default) for links that may change or be deleted.

messages.content:

shortlink's documentation that come with it. Name the document each
fact comes from. If the passages don't answer the question, say that

Passages:

[docs/security.md: Webhook signing]
If you use webhooks, set webhooks.secret and verify each delivery at the receiver. Every request carries `X-Shortlink-Signature: sha256=<hex>`, an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body keyed with webhooks.secret. Compute the same HMAC over the body you received and compare it to the header. See docs/webhooks.md for the event payloads.

[docs/webhooks.md: Verifying a signature]
Each request carries the header `X-Shortlink-Signature: sha256=<hex>`,
an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body keyed with `webhooks.secret`. To
verify it:

1. Read the raw body bytes first, before parsing them as JSON.
2. Compute HMAC-SHA256 over those bytes with `webhooks.secret`.
3. Compare the hex digest with the part of the header after `sha256=`,
   using a constant-time comparison. Reject the request if they differ.

[docs/webhooks.md: Webhooks]
Since v1.3.0, shortlink can notify an HTTP endpoint when a link changes.

[docs/architecture.md: An API request]
1. `internal/limit` rates the client as for a redirect.
2. `internal/api` reads the `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header and asks `internal/store` to match it against the `api_keys` table. The store compares the SHA-256 hash of the presented key. A missing, wrong, or revoked key is 401; a valid key whose scope doesn't allow the request is 403.
3. The key's scope decides what is allowed: `read` for GET, `write` for creating and deleting links, `admin` for reading every link's clicks across the server.
4. The handler validates the body in `internal/api`: targets must be `http` or `https` and no longer than `max_url_length` (2048 bytes), a domain in `blocked_domains` is refused with 400 and the error "domain blocked", a `slug` is 3 to 32 characters of letters, digits, and hyphens, and a slug already in use is 409 Conflict. Codes are generated by the store at `code_length` from letters and digits, minus `0`, `O`, `1`, `l`, and `I`.
5. `internal/store` writes or reads the link. A link's target cannot be changed: delete it and create it again with the same slug.
6. For `link.created` and `link.deleted`, `internal/hooks` POSTs a JSON body to `webhooks.url` when that setting is set. Each request carries `X-Shortlink-Signature: sha256=<hex>`, an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body keyed with `webhooks.secret`. Delivery failures are retried up to 5 attempts in all, waiting 1s, 2s, 4s, and 8s between them; after the last failure the event is logged and dropped, and `shortlink_webhook_failures_total` goes up. `link.expired` is sent the same way. See docs/webhooks.md.
7. `internal/api` answers with JSON. Errors carry an `error` field: 400 for an invalid body, 401 for a missing, wrong, or revoked key, 403 for a scope that doesn't allow the request, 409 for a slug in use, 429 for the rate limit.

Question: How can a webhook receiver check that a request really came from shortlink?

The steps, per docs/webhooks.md: Verifying a signature:

1. Read the raw body bytes first, before parsing them as JSON.
2. Compute HMAC-SHA256 over those bytes with `webhooks.secret`.
3. Compare the hex digest with the part of the header after `sha256=`, using a constant-time comparison. Reject the request if they differ.

```sh
shortlink migrate
```

Since v1.3.0 migrations run automatically when the server starts. The
`shortlink migrate` command applies them by hand and exits:

```sh
shortlink migrate
```

Use it to migrate without starting the server, and when upgrading from
v1.2.0 or earlier: those databases predate automatic migrations, so run
`shortlink migrate` with the new binary before starting it.

Migrations only go forward. Downgrading after a migration is not
supported; restore a backup instead. Back up before every upgrade.

input: Which setting decides how soon a new click shows up in the API, and what is its default?

messages.content:
Answer the question using only the passages from
shortlink's documentation that come with it. Name the document each
fact comes from. If the passages don't answer the question, say that
the documentation doesn't say.

Passages:

[docs/performance.md: Click counting]
Each redirect counts one click. Counts are held in memory and written to the database every `clicks.flush_interval` (5 seconds by default):

```yaml
clicks:
  flush_interval: 5s
  retention_days: 400
```

This batching has two consequences:

- **Freshness**: a new click shows up in the API within about 5 seconds of the redirect. Raise or lower `clicks.flush_interval` to trade write frequency against how stale the counts look.
- **Crashes**: a crash can lose up to one flush interval of counts. A normal shutdown writes them first, so stopping the server with SIGTERM keeps every count it has taken.

Daily click counts are kept for `clicks.retention_days` (400 by default).

[docs/faq.md: How soon do clicks show up?]
Within about 5 seconds. Clicks are held in memory and written to the database every clicks.flush_interval (5s by default), so a new click appears in the API after roughly that long. A crash can lose up to 5 seconds of counts; a normal shutdown writes them first. GET /api/links/{code} in api.md returns a link's total clicks.

[docs/redirects.md: Click counting]
Every redirect counts one click, including requests from bots. Counts are not
unique visitors; the same client following a link twice counts twice. A HEAD
request does not count.

Counts are held in memory and written to the database every
clicks.flush_interval (5s by default):

- A new click shows up in the API within about 5 seconds.
- A crash can lose up to 5 seconds of counts. A shutdown that finishes
  normally writes the pending counts first.

[docs/performance.md: Timeouts]
Three timeouts bound how long requests can take. Tune them in config/defaults.yaml or by environment variable:

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| read_timeout | 5s | Longest time to read a request |
| write_timeout | 10s | Longest time to write a response |
| shutdown_timeout | 15s | Time allowed for requests in flight when stopping |

```yaml
read_timeout: 5s
write_timeout: 10s
shutdown_timeout: 15s
```

```sh
SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT=30s shortlink serve
```

`shutdown_timeout` applies when the server stops. shortlink waits up to this long for in-flight requests to finish and writes out counted clicks before exiting. Give it longer than the slowest response you expect to serve.

According to `CHANGELOG.md`, that release introduced the ability to create a link with an `expires_at` time (along with custom short codes and CSV import/export).

Related details from the docs:
- `docs/redirects.md`: a short URL whose `expires_at` time has passed returns 404; expiry is checked on each request, and a link created with an `expires_at` already in the past is expired immediately.
- `docs/troubleshooting.md`: covers the case of a new link returning 404 because its `expires_at` was already past — check the value and its time zone.

Note: `CHANGELOG.md` v1.3.0 later added webhooks including a `link.expired` event, but the expiry feature itself came in v1.2.0.

messages.content:
[docs/short-codes.md: Custom codes]
Give a code with the `--slug` flag:

```sh
shortlink links add https://example.com/a/long/path --slug launch
```

or with the `slug` field when creating a link through the API (see
docs/api.md). A slug must be 3 to 32 characters and may contain letters,
digits, and hyphens.

If the slug is already in use, the request fails with 409 Conflict. Pick
another slug, or delete the existing link first:

```sh
shortlink links delete launch
```

The codes `api`, `admin`, `healthz`, and `metrics` are reserved and cannot
be used as slugs.

[docs/api.md: Create a link]
POST /api/links with a JSON body:

{"url": "https://example.com/a/long/path", "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z"}

expires_at and slug are optional; slug sets a custom code (see
docs/short-codes.md). The response is 201 Created with the new link:

{"code": "x7Kp2", "short_url": "https://sl.example/x7Kp2"}

[docs/cli.md: shortlink keys create `--name <name> --scope read|write|admin`]
Create an API key. The key starts with `sl_` and is shown once, at creation;
the server stores only its SHA-256 hash. Scopes are cumulative: `read` allows
GET requests, `write` also creates and deletes links, `admin` also reads every
link's clicks across the server.

```sh
shortlink keys create --name ci --scope write
```

[docs/cli.md: shortlink links add `<url>`]
Create a link and print its short URL. `--slug name` sets a custom short code
(3 to 32 characters, letters, digits, and hyphens); a slug already in use is
refused with 409 Conflict. `--expires 2027-01-01T00:00:00Z` sets the expiry
time. The target must be an http or https URL no longer than
`max_url_length`, and its domain must not be in `blocked_domains`.

```sh
shortlink links add https://example.com/a/long/path --slug launch --expires 2027-01-01T00:00:00Z
```

[docs/api.md: Create a link]
POST /api/links with a JSON body:

{"url": "https://example.com/a/long/path", "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z"}

expires_at and slug are optional; slug sets a custom code (see
docs/short-codes.md). The response is 201 Created with the new link:

{"code": "x7Kp2", "short_url": "https://sl.example/x7Kp2"}

[docs/cli.md: shortlink links add `<url>`]
Create a link and print its short URL. `--slug name` sets a custom short code
(3 to 32 characters, letters, digits, and hyphens); a slug already in use is
refused with 409 Conflict. `--expires 2027-01-01T00:00:00Z` sets the expiry
time. The target must be an http or https URL no longer than
`max_url_length`, and its domain must not be in `blocked_domains`.

```sh
shortlink links add https://example.com/a/long/path --slug launch --expires 2027-01-01T00:00:00Z
```

[docs/architecture.md: An API request]
1. `internal/limit` rates the client as for a redirect.
2. `internal/api` reads the `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header and asks `internal/store` to match it against the `api_keys` table. The store compares the SHA-256 hash of the presented key. A missing, wrong, or revoked key is 401; a valid key whose scope doesn't allow the request is 403.
3. The key's scope decides what is allowed: `read` for GET, `write` for creating and deleting links, `admin` for reading every link's clicks across the server.
4. The handler validates the body in `internal/api`: targets must be `http` or `https` and no longer than `max_url_length` (2048 bytes), a domain in `blocked_domains` is refused with 400 and the error "domain blocked", a `slug` is 3 to 32 characters of letters, digits, and hyphens, and a slug already in use is 409 Conflict. Codes are generated by the store at `code_length` from letters and digits, minus `0`, `O`, `1`, `l`, and `I`.
5. `internal/store` writes or reads the link. A link's target cannot be changed: delete it and create it again with the same slug.
6. For `link.created` and `link.deleted`, `internal/hooks` POSTs a JSON body to `webhooks.url` when that setting is set. Each request carries `X-Shortlink-Signature: sha256=<hex>`, an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body keyed with `webhooks.secret`. Delivery failures are retried up to 5 attempts in all, waiting 1s, 2s, 4s, and 8s between them; after the last failure the event is logged and dropped, and `shortlink_webhook_failures_total` goes up. `link.expired` is sent the same way. See docs/webhooks.md.
7. `internal/api` answers with JSON. Errors carry an `error` field: 400 for an invalid body, 401 for a missing, wrong, or revoked key, 403 for a scope that doesn't allow the request, 409 for a slug in use, 429 for the rate limit.

[docs/webhooks.md: Webhooks]
Since v1.3.0, shortlink can notify an HTTP endpoint when a link changes.

To create a short link via the API, send a **`POST /api/links`** request with a JSON body:

```json
{"url": "https://example.com/a/long/path", "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z"}
```

- **`url`** (required) — the target. It must be an `http` or `https` URL no longer than `max_url_length` (2048 bytes), and its domain must not be in `blocked_domains` (otherwise you get a 400 "domain blocked").
- **`expires_at`** (optional) — expiry time for the link.
- **`slug`** (optional) — a custom short code, 3–32 characters of letters, digits, and hyphens. If the slug is already in use, you get **409 Conflict**. The codes `api`, `admin`, `healthz`, and `metrics` are reserved. Without a slug, a code is generated at `code_length` from letters and digits (excluding `0`, `O`, `1`, `l`, `I`).

On success you get **201 Created** with the new link:

```json
{"code": "x7Kp2", "short_url": "https://sl.example/x7Kp2"}
```

**Authentication:** requests must carry an `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header with a valid API key (created via `shortlink keys create --name ci --scope write`). Creating links requires at least the `write` scope. A missing/invalid/revoked key returns 401, insufficient scope returns 403.

Note: a link's target cannot be changed — delete it and recreate it with the same slug instead. A `link.created` webhook event is fired if webhooks are configured.

messages.content:
[docs/configuration.md: Configuration]
shortlink reads config/defaults.yaml at startup. Any setting can be
overridden with an environment variable of the same name in capitals:
listen_addr becomes LISTEN_ADDR, and dots become underscores, so
rate_limit.burst becomes RATE_LIMIT_BURST.
Run `shortlink check-config` to load the configuration and report any
errors without starting the server.

[docs/cli.md: Command line reference]
Every command reads config/defaults.yaml. Any setting can be overridden by an
environment variable of the same name in capitals, with dots replaced by
underscores: `rate_limit.burst` becomes `RATE_LIMIT_BURST`.

[docs/metrics.md: Metrics]
shortlink serves Prometheus metrics on a separate port. Set that port with
metrics_addr (:9090 by default):

```yaml
metrics_addr: ":9090"
```

The endpoint is /metrics on metrics_addr. It is on its own port so that
metrics stay off the public port where redirects, the API, and /admin are
served. Point Prometheus at the metrics port only; do not expose it through
the reverse proxy that fronts the public port. Set metrics_addr to an empty
value to turn metrics off.

Override the port with an environment variable if needed:

```sh
METRICS_ADDR=":9191" shortlink serve
```

[docs/webhooks.md: Turning webhooks on]
Set `webhooks.url` and `webhooks.secret` in config/defaults.yaml, or the
environment variables of the same name in capitals:

```yaml
webhooks:
  url: https://ops.example/hooks/shortlink
  secret: 6f1c2f4d0a8b4e1c9f0a3b7c5d2e8f11
```

```sh
WEBHOOKS_URL=https://ops.example/hooks/shortlink
WEBHOOKS_SECRET=6f1c2f4d0a8b4e1c9f0a3b7c5d2e8f11
```

An empty `webhooks.url` turns webhooks off. The same secret is used to
sign every delivery, so keep it in sync with your receiver.

[docs/rate-limits.md: Rate limits]
Each client, identified by its IP address, may make
rate_limit.requests_per_minute requests a minute (120 by default), plus
a short burst of rate_limit.burst more (20 by default).

A client over its limit gets 429 Too Many Requests, with a Retry-After
header giving the number of seconds to wait. Redirects count against
the limit too, so a link shared widely from one office network can
exhaust that network's limit.

[docs/performance.md: Where to look next]
- rate-limits.md covers per-client request limits.
- metrics.md lists the Prometheus metrics available on `metrics_addr`.
- troubleshooting.md covers rate limits that hit everyone at once and the "database is locked" error.

[docs/api-keys.md: When a request is rejected]
A request with a missing, wrong, or revoked key gets `401 Unauthorized`. A valid key whose scope doesn't allow the request gets `403 Forbidden`: a key with `read` scope gets 403 on a request to create or delete a link, and a key with `write` scope gets 403 on a request for every link's clicks. A `429` is not a key problem; it means the client is over its rate limit. See rate-limits.md.

A failed delivery is retried, up to 5 attempts in all. The waits

messages.content:
[docs/performance.md: Click counting]
Each redirect counts one click. Counts are held in memory and written to the database every `clicks.flush_interval` (5 seconds by default):

```yaml
clicks:
  flush_interval: 5s
  retention_days: 400
```

This batching has two consequences:

- **Freshness**: a new click shows up in the API within about 5 seconds of the redirect. Raise or lower `clicks.flush_interval` to trade write frequency against how stale the counts look.
- **Crashes**: a crash can lose up to one flush interval of counts. A normal shutdown writes them first, so stopping the server with SIGTERM keeps every count it has taken.

Daily click counts are kept for `clicks.retention_days` (400 by default).

[docs/redirects.md: Click counting]
Daily counts per link are kept for clicks.retention_days (400 by default).
Read them with GET /api/links/{code}/clicks (see docs/analytics.md) or on the
admin page (see docs/admin.md). The
shortlink_redirects_total{status} metric on metrics_addr counts redirects by
status code.

[docs/analytics.md: Analytics]
Since v1.4.0, shortlink counts clicks per link per day. Daily counts are
kept for clicks.retention_days days, 400 by default, and then deleted.
The total click count for a link is kept for as long as the link exists.

GET /api/links/{code}/clicks returns the daily counts that are still
kept, oldest first.

[docs/faq.md: Are clicks unique visitors?]
No. Each redirect counts one click, bots included. The counts tell you how often a short URL was followed, not how many different people followed it. Daily counts per link are kept for clicks.retention_days (400 days). HEAD requests are answered like GET but do not count a click.

shortlink serves plain HTTP. Terminate TLS at a reverse proxy such as nginx or Caddy and point clients at the proxy. See deploy.md for the proxy setup.

When shortlink runs behind a proxy, every request appears to come from the proxy's address unless you tell it otherwise. List the proxy's address in trusted_proxies; shortlink then takes the client's address from the X-Forwarded-For header the proxy adds. list the proxy in `trusted_proxies` so rate limiting sees the real
client address.

**Set `trusted_proxies` to include your nginx proxy's address.**

What's happening: rate limits are per client IP (120 requests/minute + a burst of 20 by default), and shortlink identifies clients by IP address. Behind nginx, every request arrives from the proxy's address, so all users share one bucket and hit the limit together.

The fix, from **docs/deploy.md** ("Behind a reverse proxy") and **docs/troubleshooting.md** ("Every user hits the rate limit at once"): list the proxy's address in `trusted_proxies`. shortlink will then take the client's address from the `X-Forwarded-For` header that nginx adds, and rate limiting (and request logs) will use the real client address instead of the proxy's.

Two cautions from **docs/security.md** and **docs/admin.md**:
- Only list proxies you control — anyone who can reach shortlink while spoofing `X-Forwarded-For` from a trusted proxy address could evade rate limits.
- The same `trusted_proxies` setting matters for `/admin`, since rate limiting there also sees the real client address only once it's configured.

Note: the docs describe `trusted_proxies` conceptually but don't show the exact config-file syntax or file format for it, so consult your config file/example for how to list the addresses.

messages.content:
[docs/troubleshooting.md: A new link returns 404]
If the link was created with an expires_at time that has already
passed, it is expired from the moment it is created, and its short URL
returns 404. Check the expires_at value, including its time zone.

[docs/api.md: Create a link]
POST /api/links with a JSON body:

{"url": "https://example.com/a/long/path", "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z"}

expires_at and slug are optional; slug sets a custom code (see
docs/short-codes.md). The response is 201 Created with the new link:

{"code": "x7Kp2", "short_url": "https://sl.example/x7Kp2"}

[docs/redirects.md: Deleted and expired links]
A short URL whose link has been deleted or whose expires_at time has passed
returns 404. Expiry is checked on each request, so a link stops redirecting at
its expires_at time; a link created with an expires_at already in the past is
expired immediately (see troubleshooting.md).

Remember the 301 warning above: a browser that cached a permanent redirect may
keep going to the old target even after the link returns 404.

[docs/api.md: Read and delete a link]
GET /api/links/{code} returns the link and its total clicks.
DELETE /api/links/{code} removes it; its short URL then returns 404.

This only works while the code is free, so do the two steps close together.

the old target may be cached by browsers that have already visited the
link, and those browsers keep going there even after the link is deleted or
